newsitem.title: MEXICO: Sidek founder ousted as president.
newsitem.headline: Sidek founder ousted as president.

text.p: Troubled Mexican conglomerate Grupo Sidek has completed management changes that place Luis Rebollar as chairman of the board and strip company founder Jorge Martinez Guitron of all but a role as chief of the steel subsidiary, Rebollar said.
The changes came during a board meeting on Monday, Rebollar told Reuters in a telephone interview late Tuesday.

The diminished role for Martinez Guitron has been expected since his former post of president was left vacant following a Sidek shareholders' meeting on May 30, when the new board of directors was chosen.

"I became chairman of the board for both companies (Sidek and Grupo Situr, the tourism subsidiary) and will continue in my position as director general of Sidek," Rebollar told Reuters in a telephone interview.

Rebollar has led the restructuring of Sidek, which is heavily in debt and was delisted from the New York Stock Exchange earlier this year, but Sidek has been unable to strike a deal with creditors. The company was hammered by the Mexican economic crisis brought on by the sudden devaluation of the peso in December 1994, largely because of its heavy load of dollar-denominated debt.
Rebollar said Martinez Guitron "is no longer part of Sidek and Situr" and will concentrate only on the steel business Grupo Simec.
Luis Garcia Limon was named as general director of Simec.

In other management changes, Arturo Perez Courtade, who has run Sidek's legal department, becomes secretary of the board, and Jose Julian Franco will continue as assistant general director of Sidek under Rebollar.
Franco will "orient himself toward the restructuring, but he has the option of choosing ... whether he wants that kind of position," Rebollar said. "He hasn't made a decision yet."
Miguel Brinkman Stockton became assistant director general of the of the Situr subsidiary, Rebollar said.
